evidence_boundary.initial_llm: source outcomes and public target conditions only
evidence_boundary.reflection_llm: source evidence plus executed initial target observations only
evidence_boundary.unrevealed_target_outcomes: never exposed to either LLM stage

gate.interpretation: The LLM may revise or stop a transfer hypothesis, but a follow-up candidate spends budget only when it is acquisition-equivalent to the target GP incumbent under the frozen zero-loss gate.

per_task.revised_hypothesis: For Morpholine-AlPhos, moderate base equivalents (~1.1-1.5) and high temperature (~100 C) with long residence times yield moderate product formation, but the maximum achievable yield is lower than in Aniline-AlPhos or Benzamide-AlPhos campaigns. Lower temperature and shorter residence time conditions are suboptimal. The optimal base identity may differ from BTMG, and exploring alternative bases such as BTTP or MTBD could improve yields. Therefore, further exploration of base identity and residence time at high temperature is necessary to identify improved conditions.
per_task.evidence_interpretation: The initial target results show that the high-temperature candidates with moderate base equivalents and long residence times (candidates 018 and 009) yield moderate outcomes (~38-39%), which is lower than the high yields observed in the source AlPhos campaigns with Aniline and Benzamide substrates. The low-temperature candidate 001 with lower temperature and shorter residence time performed poorly (~1.3%). This partially supports the hypothesis that high temperature and moderate base equivalents are favorable, but the absolute yields are much lower than expected from source data, indicating substrate-specific effects. The poor performance of candidate 001 supports the temperature sensitivity aspect. However, the moderate yields of candidates 018 and 009 contradict the expectation that at least one high-temperature candidate would outperform the lower-temperature anchor significantly. This suggests that the transfer of the same-precatalyst high-temperature regime from Aniline/Benzamide to Morpholine is only partially valid and that Morpholine-AlPhos may have different optimal conditions or base preferences.

per_task.revised_hypothesis: In the Morpholine–tBuBrettPhos target, high initial yield is not likely to be achieved with the same-precatalyst-supported region defined by strong, non-nucleophilic organic bases at high temperature, suggesting that Morpholine may have a distinct reactivity profile that requires different conditions or base identities.
per_task.evidence_interpretation: The revealed outcomes for the selected candidates (022, 029, 027) show significantly low yields (2.1292, 12.2435, and 0.2391 respectively), contradicting the original hypothesis that high yields would be achieved in the same-precatalyst-supported region with strong bases at high temperatures. The results indicate that Morpholine may not respond favorably to the same conditions that worked for other substrates like Aniline or Benzamide.

per_task.revised_hypothesis: In the Morpholine–tBuBrettPhos target, conditions using strong amidine bases do not consistently yield high outcomes at 100 °C, and alternative conditions or bases may be necessary to achieve better results.
per_task.evidence_interpretation: The revealed outcomes for the selected candidates indicate that the yields are significantly lower than expected. Candidate 005 yielded 0.6856, candidate 002 yielded 8.1462, and candidate 010 yielded 4.6714, all of which are far below the anticipated performance based on the original hypothesis. This contradicts the expectation that strong non-nucleophilic amidine bases at 100 °C would outperform other conditions.

per_task.revised_hypothesis: For Phenethylamine with AlPhos, BTTP is the leading base family, and high yield is accessible at 100 C across more than one residence-time regime. A falsifiable refinement is that BTTP will remain superior to non-BTTP options even when compared against the strongest remaining BTMG alternative; specifically, a second 100 C BTTP condition with shorter residence time should still perform at least as well as, or better than, a high-ranking 100 C long-residence BTMG condition. This hypothesis is falsified if the selected BTMG follow-up matches or exceeds the selected BTTP follow-up.
per_task.evidence_interpretation: The initial target results strongly support the core same-substrate transfer claim that BTTP is highly competitive for Phenethylamine with AlPhos under 100 C conditions: the BTTP anchor (baumgartner_cn_phenethylamine_alphos_020) gave 97.2303, clearly outperforming the two non-BTTP probes. The results also show that not all strong-source bases transfer equally well here: BTMG at similar high-temperature/long-residence conditions was good but inferior (75.2105), while DBU was poor (29.1735). This directly contradicts the part of the original mechanism that treated DBU and BTMG as comparably plausible alternatives to BTTP in this region. The evidence therefore supports a revised view in which same-substrate base identity transfers better than same-precatalyst base preferences, but it does not yet establish whether BTTP is uniquely optimal or whether optimized BTMG can still match it elsewhere in the remaining design space.

per_task.revised_hypothesis: For the 3-Chloropyridine Suzuki target, source evidence from the same substrate will transfer such that P2L1 XPhos Cl candidates in the high-temperature, high-precatalyst-fraction region are likely to give good initial yields, but residence time may also play a significant role, potentially challenging the dominance of temperature.
per_task.evidence_interpretation: The revealed results show that candidate 024 from the P2L1 XPhos Cl group performed well (85.4755), supporting the hypothesis that high temperature and high precatalyst fraction are beneficial. However, candidate 039 from the P1L1 XPhos OMs group also performed well (80.6121) under slightly lower temperature and higher residence time, suggesting that the temperature trend may not be as dominant as initially thought. This indicates a potential contradiction regarding the importance of temperature versus residence time.

interpretation: The LLM now participates in hypothesis generation, experiment design, evidence interpretation, hypothesis revision, counterexample planning, and stop decisions. The strict gate preserved the earlier routed performance; the new reflection stage is mechanistically richer but does not yet add an independent aggregate performance gain on this retrospective suite.
